references.gist: Qarun's display of wealth draws envy from some, while those given knowledge respond that Allah's reward for faith and patience is better.

chapters.heading: Swallowed by the Earth
chapters.narrative: Allah caused the earth to swallow Qarun and his home, and he had no company to aid him against Allah, nor could he defend himself. Those who had envied his position the day before then said, 'Allah extends provision to whom He wills of His servants, and restricts it. Had Allah not been gracious to us, He could have caused the earth to swallow us too.'

references.label: Surah Al-Qasas 28:81-82
references.gist: The earth swallows Qarun and his home, leaving no one able to help him, and those who had envied him recognize how easily the same fate could have been theirs.

name: The Man Who Passed a Ruined Town
summary: An unnamed man passed by a town fallen into ruin and questioned how Allah could bring it back to life; Allah caused him to 'die' for a hundred years, then raised him and showed him his untouched food, his donkey's bones, and made him a sign for people.

references.label: Surah Al-Baqarah 2:259
references.gist: A man who doubts how Allah could revive a ruined town is made to 'die' a hundred years, then is raised and shown proof through his preserved food and his donkey's bones.

tale.intro: Neither the man nor the town is named by the Quran; both are left unidentified, and the account is told as a single continuous verse.

chapters.heading: How Will Allah Bring This to Life?
chapters.narrative: The Quran gives the example of one who passed by a township that had fallen into ruin and asked, 'How will Allah bring this to life after its death?' So Allah caused him to die for a hundred years, then revived him.

references.label: Surah Al-Baqarah 2:259
references.gist: A man questions how a ruined town could be brought back to life, and Allah causes him to die for a hundred years before reviving him.

chapters.heading: A Sign for the People
chapters.narrative: Allah asked him how long he had remained; he answered a day or part of a day. He was told, 'Rather, you have remained a hundred years. Look at your food and your drink - they have not spoiled - and look at your donkey, and We will make you a sign for the people. And look at the bones, how We raise them and then clothe them with flesh.' When it became clear to him, he said, 'I know that Allah is over all things competent.'

references.label: Surah Al-Baqarah 2:259
references.gist: The man is shown his food untouched by a century's passing and his donkey's bones being restored to life, and he declares Allah's power over all things.

name: The Man of the Two Gardens
summary: A wealthy man boasted over his two flourishing gardens to his believing companion, denied the Hour would ever come, and was warned - before his gardens were destroyed and he was left in regret.

references.label: Surah Al-Kahf 18:32-44
references.gist: A parable of two men, one given two fruitful gardens who grows arrogant and denies the Hour, is warned by his companion, and loses everything when the gardens are destroyed.

tale.intro: Neither man in this parable is named by the Quran.

chapters.heading: Two Flourishing Gardens
chapters.narrative: Allah gives the example of two men, one of whom was granted two gardens of grapevines, bordered with palm trees and crops between them, each producing its fruit without fail, with a river flowing through them. Having such fruit, he told his companion, boasting, 'I am greater than you in wealth and mightier in men.' He entered his garden while wronging himself, saying, 'I do not think this will ever perish, nor do I think the Hour is coming. And even if I am returned to my Lord, I will surely find better than this in exchange.'

references.label: Surah Al-Kahf 18:32-36
references.gist: A wealthy man boasts over his two flourishing gardens, denies his gardens could ever perish or that the Hour will come, and claims he would find even better if returned to Allah.

chapters.heading: His Companion's Warning
chapters.narrative: His companion, while conversing with him, said, 'Have you disbelieved in He who created you from dust, then from a sperm-drop, then proportioned you as a man? As for me, He is Allah, my Lord, and I do not associate anyone with my Lord. Why, when you entered your garden, did you not say, "What Allah has willed; there is no power except in Allah"? Even though you see me lesser than you in wealth and children, it may be that my Lord will give me something better than your garden, and send upon it a calamity from the sky, so it becomes a smooth, dusty ground, or its water sinks into the earth so that you could never reach it again.'

references.label: Surah Al-Kahf 18:37-41
references.gist: The believing companion rebukes the man's disbelief and arrogance, reminds him to credit Allah rather than himself, and warns his garden could be destroyed.

chapters.heading: Ruin and Regret
chapters.narrative: His fruits were indeed struck down, and he began wringing his hands in dismay over all he had spent on it, as it lay collapsed upon its trellises, saying, 'Oh, I wish I had not associated anyone with my Lord.' He had no company to help him against Allah, nor could he help himself. The Quran concludes that all authority belongs to Allah, the Truth; He is best in reward and best in outcome.

references.label: Surah Al-Kahf 18:42-44
references.gist: The man's gardens are destroyed, leaving him in regret for his earlier arrogance and disbelief, with the passage closing on the truth that all authority belongs to Allah alone.

name: The People of the Ditch (Ashab al-Ukhdud)
summary: Believers were thrown into a trench of fire for their faith by a persecuting people who sat and watched; the Quran condemns those who did this, and a hadith in Sahih Muslim preserves a fuller narrative of a boy, a king, a sorcerer, and a monk behind the episode.

references.label: Surah Al-Buruj 85:4-8
references.gist: The Quran condemns the companions of the trench of fire, who sat watching what they did to the believers and resented them only for their faith in Allah.

references.label: Sahih Muslim 3005
references.gist: A long narration attributed to the Prophet (SAW) telling of a boy, a king, a sorcerer, and a monk, and the digging of trenches of fire for those who would not renounce their faith.

tale.intro: The Quran's own account of this episode is very brief; the fuller narrative context comes from a hadith rather than the Quran itself, and is presented here as such.

chapters.heading: The Trench of Fire
chapters.narrative: The Quran curses the companions of the trench - the fire, full of fuel - as they sat by it, witnesses to what they were doing to the believers. It states they resented the believers for no reason except that they believed in Allah, the Exalted in Might, the Praiseworthy.

references.label: Surah Al-Buruj 85:4-8
references.gist: The companions of the trench are condemned for burning believers alive, watching it happen, and resenting them only for their faith in Allah.

chapters.heading: The Boy, the King, and the Monk
chapters.narrative: A long hadith in Sahih Muslim, narrated on the authority of Suhayb, tells of a king who had a sorcerer, who in his old age asked the king to send him a boy to train as his successor. On his way to the sorcerer, the boy began passing a monk and was drawn to his faith, coming to believe in Allah in secret. The boy was later granted the ability, by Allah's permission, to cure blindness and leprosy, and a companion of the king who had gone blind was healed after affirming faith in the boy's Lord. When the king learned that his companion now attributed his healing to a Lord other than the king himself, he tortured the man until he named the boy, then turned on the monk and the boy as well.

references.label: Sahih Muslim 3005
references.gist: A boy trained under a sorcerer is drawn to faith by a monk, gains the ability to heal by Allah's permission, and is pursued by the king once his faith becomes known.

chapters.heading: The Ditches Are Dug
chapters.narrative: According to the same hadith, the king's attempts to kill the boy repeatedly failed by Allah's protection, until the boy told the king that he could only be killed if the king gathered the people, tied him to a tree trunk, and shot him with an arrow while saying, 'In the name of the Lord of this boy.' The king did so, and the boy died - but the people who witnessed it declared, 'We believe in the Lord of the boy.' Enraged, the king ordered trenches dug and filled with fire at the roads, commanding that anyone who would not renounce their faith be thrown into them. This hadith is understood to supply the narrative background the Quran's brief condemnation in Surah Al-Buruj refers to.

references.label: Sahih Muslim 3005
references.gist: After the boy's death draws public declarations of faith, the king orders trenches of fire dug and commands that anyone refusing to renounce their belief be thrown in.

name: Maryam (Mary), Mother of Isa
summary: Maryam was dedicated to Allah's service before her birth, raised under Zakariya's guardianship, and chosen and purified above the women of creation; she later withdrew to a place in the east, where an angel announced to her the coming of a son.

references.label: Surah Ali 'Imran 3:33-37, 42-44
references.gist: Maryam's mother dedicates her to Allah's service, she is raised under Zakariya's guardianship, and chosen above the women of creation.

references.label: Surah Maryam 19:16-21
references.gist: Maryam withdraws to a place in the east and receives the angel's announcement of a son.

tale.intro: The birth of Isa and his infancy are told in fuller depth in his own tale on this site; this account keeps its focus on Maryam herself.

chapters.heading: A Mother's Vow
chapters.narrative: The wife of Imran said, 'My Lord, I have pledged to You what is in my womb, dedicated for Your service, so accept this from me.' When she delivered a daughter, she said, 'My Lord, I have delivered a female,' and Allah knew best what she had delivered, for 'the male is not like the female.' She named her Maryam, and asked Allah's protection for her and her offspring from Satan.

references.label: Surah Ali 'Imran 3:35-36
references.gist: Maryam's mother vows to dedicate the child in her womb to Allah's service before her birth, and names her Maryam, seeking Allah's protection for her from Satan.

chapters.heading: Raised Under Zakariya's Care
chapters.narrative: Allah accepted her with good acceptance, caused her to grow in a good manner, and placed her in the care of Zakariya. Every time he entered upon her in the prayer chamber, he found provision with her. He asked, 'O Maryam, from where does this come to you?' She answered, 'It is from Allah - indeed, Allah provides for whom He wills without account.'

references.label: Surah Ali 'Imran 3:37
references.gist: Maryam is raised under Zakariya's guardianship, and he repeatedly finds provision with her in the prayer chamber that she attributes directly to Allah.

chapters.heading: Chosen and Purified Above the Women of Creation
chapters.narrative: The angels said, 'O Maryam, indeed Allah has chosen you and purified you, and chosen you above the women of the worlds. O Maryam, be devoutly obedient to your Lord, prostrate, and bow with those who bow.' The Quran adds that this news of the unseen was revealed to the Prophet (SAW), since he was not present when the guardians cast their pens to decide who would care for her.

references.label: Surah Ali 'Imran 3:42-44
references.gist: Angels tell Maryam that Allah has chosen and purified her above the women of creation and instruct her to devote herself to worship.

chapters.heading: Withdrawing to a Place in the East
chapters.narrative: Maryam withdrew from her family to a place toward the east, and took a screen to seclude herself from them.

references.label: Surah Maryam 19:16-17
references.gist: Maryam withdraws from her family to a secluded place in the east.

chapters.heading: The Angel's Announcement
chapters.narrative: Allah sent His angel to her, who appeared to her as a well-proportioned man. She said, 'I seek refuge in the Most Merciful from you, if you fear Allah.' He said, 'I am only the messenger of your Lord, to give you news of a pure boy.' She asked, 'How can I have a boy when no man has touched me, and I have not been unchaste?' He answered, 'Thus it will be; your Lord says, it is easy for Me, and We will make him a sign to the people and a mercy from Us. It is a matter already decreed.'

references.label: Surah Maryam 19:18-21
references.gist: An angel appears to Maryam in the form of a man and announces she will bear a pure son despite having been touched by no man, calling it an easy and already-decreed matter for Allah.

name: The Two Sons of Adam
summary: Adam's (AS) two sons each offered a sacrifice to Allah; when one's offering was accepted and the other's was not, the rejected brother grew jealous and threatened to kill him. His brother refused to raise a hand against him in return, out of fear of Allah, but was killed anyway, becoming the first murder among mankind. Not knowing what to do with the body, the killer watched a crow scratch the ground to bury another crow, and realized he could do the same for his brother. Neither son is named in the Quran or in any authentic hadith.

references.label: Surah Al-Ma'idah 5:27-31
references.gist: Recounts the two offerings, the rejected brother's threat, the other's refusal to retaliate, the murder, and the crow that showed the killer how to bury the body.

chapters.heading: Two Offerings
chapters.narrative: Adam's two sons each brought an offering to Allah. One was accepted and the other was not, and the one whose offering was rejected said, 'I will surely kill you.' His brother answered that Allah only accepts the offering of the God-conscious, and that even if he raised his hand to kill him, he would not raise his own hand against him in return, for he feared Allah, the Lord of all worlds.

references.label: Surah Al-Ma'idah 5:27-28
references.gist: One brother's offering is accepted and the other's is not; the rejected brother threatens to kill him, and is told Allah only accepts from the God-conscious.

chapters.heading: The First Murder
chapters.narrative: The brother said he would rather let him bear the sin of killing him, alongside his own sin, than raise a hand against him, so that he would be among the companions of the Fire, which is the reward of wrongdoers. His own soul allowed him to kill his brother, and he killed him, becoming one of the losers.

references.label: Surah Al-Ma'idah 5:29-30
references.gist: One brother tells the other he would rather he bear the sin alone than retaliate; the other's soul permits him to kill his brother, and he does, becoming a loser.

chapters.heading: The Crow's Lesson
chapters.narrative: Not knowing how to deal with his brother's corpse, Allah sent a crow to scratch at the ground, showing him how to bury it. He said, 'Woe to me, was I unable to be like this crow and bury my brother's body?' and became full of regret.

references.label: Surah Al-Ma'idah 5:31
references.gist: Allah sends a crow to scratch the ground, showing the killer how to bury his brother's body, and he is filled with regret.

name: The Cow (Al-Baqarah)
summary: Musa (AS) told his people Allah commanded them to sacrifice a cow, after a murder among them that no one would confess to. Rather than simply obeying, they repeatedly questioned him about its exact age and color, delaying until they finally found and slaughtered one matching the description. Allah then commanded them to strike the murdered man with part of it, and he was restored to life to identify his killer, a sign of Allah's power over life and death that the surah Al-Baqarah, the Cow, is named after.

references.label: Surah Al-Baqarah 2:67-73
references.gist: Musa relays Allah's command to sacrifice a cow; the people repeatedly question its description before complying, and the slain man is struck with part of it and speaks, revealing his killer.

chapters.heading: A Command Met With Questions
chapters.narrative: Musa told his people that Allah commanded them to sacrifice a cow. They accused him of mocking them, and when he insisted it was a serious command, they asked him to specify its age. He said it should be neither old nor young, but in between. They then asked its color, and he said a bright yellow cow, pleasing to those who look at it.

references.label: Surah Al-Baqarah 2:67-69
references.gist: Musa conveys the command to sacrifice a cow; his people repeatedly press him for its exact age and color before agreeing to comply.

chapters.heading: Delay Upon Delay
chapters.narrative: Still unsatisfied, they asked him to describe it further, since to them cows looked alike. Musa said it should be a cow not broken in to plow the earth or irrigate the field, sound and without blemish. They finally said he had now brought the truth, and they slaughtered it, though they almost did not do it.

references.label: Surah Al-Baqarah 2:70-71
references.gist: The people ask for yet more detail before Musa describes an unblemished cow never used for labor, and they finally slaughter it, though they had nearly refused.

chapters.heading: The Dead Man Speaks
chapters.narrative: This command followed a killing among them, over which they disputed and each side accused the other, while Allah brought out what they concealed. Allah commanded them to strike the slain man with part of the cow, and just as He brings the dead to life, He showed them His signs so that they might understand.

references.label: Surah Al-Baqarah 2:72-73
references.gist: The command follows an unresolved killing; the people are told to strike the dead man with part of the cow, and Allah reveals what they had concealed, a sign of His power to give life.

name: Modesty and Covering (Hijab)
summary: The Quran instructs both believing men and believing women to lower their gaze and guard their private parts, and additionally instructs believing women to draw their headcovers over their chests and, elsewhere, to draw their outer garments close around themselves when out in public, so they may be recognized as believing women and not be harassed.

references.label: Surah An-Nur 24:30-31
references.gist: Instructs believing men and believing women alike to lower their gaze and guard their private parts, and additionally instructs women to draw their headcovers over their chests.

references.label: Surah Al-Ahzab 33:59
references.gist: Instructs the Prophet's wives, daughters, and the believing women to draw their outer garments close around themselves so they may be recognized and not harassed.

name: Minor Signs of the Hour
summary: Distinct from the major signs elsewhere in this section (Ad-Dukhan, Al-Mahdi, Ad-Dajjal, and the rest), the Prophet also described a long-running set of smaller signs building toward the Hour: religious knowledge decreasing as scholars die, ignorance spreading, open sexual immorality becoming widespread, and women coming to greatly outnumber men. The very hadith that establishes the six articles of faith closes with one more: barefoot, destitute shepherds competing to build ever taller structures.

references.label: Sahih al-Bukhari 81
references.gist: Anas ibn Malik narrates signs of the Hour: religious knowledge decreasing, ignorance prevailing, open sexual immorality becoming widespread, and women greatly outnumbering men.

references.label: Sahih al-Bukhari 50
references.gist: The same hadith that establishes the six articles of faith ends with Jibril asking about the Hour, and the Prophet naming one sign: barefoot, naked, destitute shepherds competing to build tall structures.

name: The Jinn Who Listened to the Quran
summary: A group of jinn overheard the Prophet reciting Quran, were struck by it, and returned to their own people as warners, telling them they had heard a wondrous recitation guiding to what is right, and that they now believed in it.

references.label: Surah Al-Jinn 72:1-2
references.gist: Jinn who overheard the Quran being recited describe it to their people as a wondrous recitation guiding to what is right, and say they have believed in it.

references.label: Surah Al-Ahqaf 46:29-32
references.gist: A parallel account: a group of jinn is directed to listen to the Prophet's recitation, and they return to their people as warners calling them to believe.

name: The Names of Allah (Al-Asma Al-Husna)
summary: The Quran instructs believers to call upon Allah by His most beautiful names, and the Prophet taught that Allah has ninety-nine names, one hundred less one, and that whoever preserves them will enter Paradise.

references.label: Surah Al-A'raf 7:180
references.gist: Allah has the most beautiful names, so call upon Him by them, and keep away from those who abuse His names.

references.label: Sahih al-Bukhari 2736
references.gist: Allah has ninety-nine names, one hundred less one, and whoever preserves them will enter Paradise.

name: Shirk (Associating Partners With Allah)
summary: The Quran states Allah does not forgive shirk, associating partners with Him in worship, though He forgives anything less than that to whom He wills. The Prophet named it first when asked to identify the greatest of the major sins.

references.label: Surah An-Nisa 4:48
references.gist: States Allah does not forgive that partners be associated with Him, but forgives what is less than that to whom He wills.

references.label: Sahih al-Bukhari 6919
references.gist: Asked to name the greatest of the major sins, the Prophet named associating partners with Allah first, then undutifulness to parents, then false testimony.

name: Nifaq (Hypocrisy)
summary: The Prophet described the signs of a hypocrite: when he speaks he lies, when he promises he breaks it, and when he is entrusted he betrays that trust. An entire surah, Al-Munafiqun, addresses this condition directly.

references.label: Sahih al-Bukhari 33
references.gist: The signs of a hypocrite are three: when he speaks he lies, when he promises he breaks it, when he is entrusted he betrays.

references.label: Surah Al-Munafiqun 63:1-8
references.gist: An entire surah describing the hypocrites, who testify with their tongues what is not in their hearts.

name: The Ruh (Spirit or Soul)
summary: When asked about the ruh, the Quran's answer is deliberately limited: it is of the affairs of the Prophet's Lord, and mankind has been given only a little knowledge of it. The site does not go beyond this stated limit.

references.label: Surah Al-Isra 17:85
references.gist: When asked about the ruh, the Prophet is told to say it is of the affairs of his Lord, and mankind has been given only a little knowledge of it.

name: Fitrah (Natural Disposition)
summary: The Prophet taught that every child is born upon fitrah, a natural disposition toward true faith, and it is the child's upbringing that turns them toward Judaism, Christianity, or Magianism.

references.label: Sahih al-Bukhari 1358
references.gist: Every child is born upon fitrah; it is his parents who make him a Jew, a Christian, or a Magian.

name: Taqwa (God-Consciousness)
summary: The Quran states directly that the most noble among people in Allah's sight is the one with the most taqwa, God-consciousness, not lineage, wealth, or tribe.

references.label: Surah Al-Hujurat 49:13
references.gist: States the most noble of people in Allah's sight is the most righteous, taqwa, among them.

name: Tawakkul (Reliance on Allah)
summary: The Quran states that whoever places their reliance on Allah will find Him sufficient, a promise made directly in the same passage discussing provision coming from where one does not expect.

references.label: Surah At-Talaq 65:3
references.gist: States that whoever relies upon Allah, He is sufficient for him.

name: Sabr (Patience)
summary: The Quran instructs believers to seek help through patience and prayer, and states plainly that Allah is with those who are patient.

references.label: Surah Al-Baqarah 2:153
references.gist: Instructs believers to seek help through patience and prayer, stating Allah is with the patient.

name: Eid Prayers
summary: The Prophet, Abu Bakr, and Umar prayed the two Eid prayers before delivering the sermon, establishing the order followed since: the prayer comes first, then the khutbah.

references.label: Sahih al-Bukhari 963
references.gist: Ibn Umar narrates that Allah's Messenger, Abu Bakr, and Umar used to offer the two Eid prayers before delivering the sermon.

name: Zakat al-Fitr
summary: The Prophet made Zakat al-Fitr obligatory on every Muslim, slave or free, male or female, young or old, one sa' of dates or one sa' of barley, to be paid before people go out to the Eid prayer.

references.label: Sahih al-Bukhari 1503
references.gist: The Prophet made Zakat al-Fitr obligatory on every Muslim, a sa' of dates or barley, to be paid before the Eid prayer.

name: Qiyam al-Layl (Night Prayer)
summary: The Quran commands the Prophet to pray in part of the night as an additional act of worship, and the Prophet taught that the most excellent prayer after the obligatory prayers is prayer during the night.

references.label: Surah Al-Isra 17:79
references.gist: Commands prayer in part of the night as an additional act of worship, with the promise of a praised station.

references.label: Sahih Muslim 1163
references.gist: The most excellent prayer after the obligatory prayers is prayer during the night.

name: Voluntary Fasting
summary: Beyond Ramadan, the Prophet taught that fasting six days of Shawwal after Ramadan is like fasting the whole year, and that fasting the day of Ashura expiates the sins of the preceding year.

references.label: Sahih Muslim 1164a
references.gist: Whoever fasts Ramadan then follows it with six days of Shawwal, it is as if he fasted for a lifetime.

references.label: Sahih Muslim 1162
references.gist: The Prophet hoped that fasting the day of Ashura would expiate the sins of the preceding year.

name: Udhiyah (Eid al-Adha Sacrifice)
summary: The Quran commands praying to one's Lord and sacrificing to Him alone. The Prophet taught that the order on Eid al-Adha is prayer first, then sacrifice, and that slaughtering beforehand does not count as the sacrifice.

references.label: Surah Al-Kawthar 108:1-2
references.gist: Commands the Prophet to pray to his Lord and sacrifice to Him alone.

references.label: Sahih al-Bukhari 5545
references.gist: The first thing to do on the day of Eid al-Adha is pray, then return to slaughter the sacrifice; slaughtering beforehand does not count as the sacrifice.

name: Umrah
summary: The Prophet taught that one Umrah to the next is an expiation for whatever sins came between them, and that the reward of an accepted Hajj is nothing less than Paradise.

references.label: Sahih al-Bukhari 1773
references.gist: One Umrah to the next is an expiation for the sins committed between them, and an accepted Hajj's only reward is Paradise.

name: Istikhara (Prayer for Guidance)
summary: The Prophet taught his companions to seek Allah's guidance in all matters just as he taught them a surah of the Quran, through a short prayer followed by a specific dua asking Allah to ordain the matter if it is good, or turn it away if it is not.

references.label: Sahih al-Bukhari 1166
references.gist: The Prophet taught the companions Istikhara for all matters as he taught them a surah, with a specific dua asking Allah to ordain a matter if good and turn it away if not.

name: Dua Upon Calamity
summary: The Quran teaches saying 'to Allah we belong and to Him we return' upon affliction. The Prophet taught adding a request that Allah reward the affliction and replace it with something better, a dua Umm Salamah recited after her husband's death.

references.label: Surah Al-Baqarah 2:156
references.gist: Teaches saying, to Allah we belong and to Him we will return, upon affliction.

references.label: Sahih Muslim 918a
references.gist: Teaches adding, O Allah, reward me for my affliction and replace it for me with something better, a dua Umm Salamah recited after her husband Abu Salamah's death.

name: The Rights of a Muslim Over Another Muslim
summary: The Prophet enumerated specific rights one Muslim owes another: returning a greeting, responding to an invitation, saying 'yarhamuk Allah' when someone sneezes and praises Allah, visiting the sick, and following a funeral.

references.label: Sahih Muslim 2162
references.gist: The rights of a Muslim over another Muslim: return his greeting, accept his invitation, say 'yarhamuk Allah' when he sneezes and praises Allah, visit him when sick, and follow his funeral.

name: Rights of Workers
summary: The Prophet named one who hires a laborer, gets full work from him, then withholds his wages, as one of three people Allah Himself will oppose on the Day of Resurrection.

references.label: Sahih al-Bukhari 2227
references.gist: Allah says He will be an opponent on the Day of Resurrection to one who hires a laborer, gets full work from him, and does not pay his wages.

name: Qisas (Retaliation)
summary: The Quran establishes retaliation for murder and injury, a life for a life and equal retaliation for wounds, while also making forgiveness or a settled compensation a lawful, encouraged alternative.

references.label: Surah Al-Baqarah 2:178-179
references.gist: Establishes the law of retaliation for killing, while allowing forgiveness and fair compensation as an alternative, calling it a mercy.

references.label: Surah Al-Ma'idah 5:45
references.gist: States the law given to the Children of Israel: a life for a life, an eye for an eye, and equal retaliation for wounds, with forgiveness as an atonement.

name: False Testimony
summary: Asked to name the greatest of the major sins, the Prophet listed associating partners with Allah, undutifulness to parents, and false testimony, repeating the warning until the companions wished he would stop.

references.label: Sahih al-Bukhari 6919
references.gist: The Prophet names the greatest major sins as shirk, undutifulness to parents, and false testimony, repeating it until the companions wished he would stop.

name: Marriage and Divorce Basics
summary: The Quran requires a husband to give his wife her dowry as a gift, sets divorce as revocable twice, after which a husband must either retain his wife honorably or release her with grace, and requires counting the waiting period accurately.

references.label: Surah An-Nisa 4:4
references.gist: Instructs giving women their due dowries as a gift.

references.label: Surah Al-Baqarah 2:229
references.gist: States divorce is revocable twice, after which a husband must retain his wife honorably or release her with grace.

references.label: Surah At-Talaq 65:1
references.gist: Instructs counting the waiting period accurately and not expelling a wife from her home during it except for clear misconduct.

name: Writing Down Debts
summary: The longest verse in the Quran instructs believers to put a fixed-term debt in writing, with witnesses, so nothing is disputed later.

references.label: Surah Al-Baqarah 2:282
references.gist: The Quran's longest verse, instructing that a debt for a fixed term be put in writing with witnesses.

name: Al-Mu'aqqibat, the Guarding Angels
summary: The Quran describes successive angels stationed before and behind each person, protecting them by Allah's command, distinct from the Kiraman Katibin, who record rather than guard.

references.label: Surah Ar-Ra'd 13:11
references.gist: States that for each person there are successive angels before and behind, protecting them by Allah's command.

name: Angels Who Seek Out Gatherings of Remembrance
summary: The Prophet taught that Allah has angels who travel the roads seeking out gatherings where He is remembered, calling to one another to come, and surrounding the gathering with their wings up to the lowest heaven.

references.label: Sahih al-Bukhari 6408
references.gist: Allah has angels who travel the roads seeking gatherings of remembrance, calling each other to it, and surrounding it with their wings up to the lowest heaven.

name: The Devils Chained in Ramadan
summary: The Prophet taught that when Ramadan begins, the gates of Paradise are opened, the gates of Hell are closed, and the devils are chained.

references.label: Sahih al-Bukhari 1899
references.gist: When Ramadan begins, the gates of Paradise are opened, the gates of Hell are closed, and the devils are chained.

name: The Sabbath-Breakers
summary: A community was tested by fish that appeared abundantly only on the Sabbath, the day they had been commanded to keep, and disappeared on other days. Those who transgressed by fishing on the Sabbath anyway were told, 'be disgraced apes.'

references.label: Surah Al-A'raf 7:163-166
references.gist: A coastal town is tested by fish appearing only on the Sabbath; those who transgress and fish anyway are told to be disgraced apes.

references.label: Surah Al-Baqarah 2:65
references.gist: A parallel, shorter reference to those among the Children of Israel who transgressed the Sabbath and were told to be disgraced apes.

name: Those Who Fled Death
summary: A group of people, in the thousands, fled their homes out of fear of death. Allah said to them, 'die,' and then gave them life again, a sign of His power over life and death addressed directly to the Prophet.

references.label: Surah Al-Baqarah 2:243
references.gist: Those who fled their homes in the thousands out of fear of death are told by Allah to die, then are given life again.

name: Laylat al-Qadr (The Night of Decree)
summary: The Quran states it was sent down on the Night of Decree, and that this night is better than a thousand months. The Prophet taught that whoever stands in prayer on it out of faith, seeking reward, is forgiven what came before, and told his companions to search for it in the odd nights of the last ten of Ramadan.

references.label: Surah Al-Qadr 97:1-5
references.gist: States the Quran was sent down on the Night of Decree, and that this night is better than a thousand months.

references.label: Sahih al-Bukhari 2014
references.gist: Whoever stands in prayer on the Night of Decree out of sincere faith, seeking reward, is forgiven his previous sins.

references.label: Sahih al-Bukhari 2017
references.gist: Search for the Night of Decree in the odd nights of the last ten nights of Ramadan.

name: The Preservation of the Quran
summary: The Quran states that Allah Himself sent down the Reminder and that He is the one who will preserve it.

references.label: Surah Al-Hijr 15:9
references.gist: States that Allah sent down the Reminder and that He will preserve it.

name: Why the Quran Came Gradually
summary: The Quran records the objection that it should have been sent down all at once, and answers it directly: it was revealed in stages to make the Prophet's heart firm, and recited at a deliberate pace.

references.label: Surah Al-Furqan 25:32
references.gist: Answers the objection that the Quran should have come all at once: it was sent in stages to make the Prophet's heart firm, at a measured pace.

name: The Challenge to Produce a Surah Like It
summary: The Quran addresses those in doubt about what was revealed with a direct challenge: produce a single surah like it, and call whatever helpers you have besides Allah, if you are truthful.

references.label: Surah Al-Baqarah 2:23
references.gist: Challenges those in doubt to produce a surah like it and call their helpers besides Allah, if they are truthful.

name: Surah Al-Fatihah
summary: The Prophet described Al-Fatihah as the greatest surah in the Quran, identifying it as the seven oft-repeated verses and the Magnificent Quran that was given to him.

references.label: Sahih al-Bukhari 5006
references.gist: The Prophet names Al-Fatihah the greatest surah in the Quran, the seven oft-repeated verses and the Magnificent Quran given to him.

name: Ayat al-Kursi, the Greatest Verse
summary: Asked which verse of the Quran was greatest, Ubayy ibn Ka'b answered Ayat al-Kursi, and the Prophet struck his chest and congratulated him on his knowledge. Its use as nightly protection is covered separately in Duas.

references.label: Sahih Muslim 810
references.gist: The Prophet asks Ubayy ibn Ka'b which verse of the Quran is greatest; when he answers Ayat al-Kursi, the Prophet affirms it and congratulates him.

name: Surah Al-Ikhlas
summary: The Prophet taught that Surah Al-Ikhlas, 'Say: He is Allah, One,' is equal to a third of the Quran.

references.label: Sahih al-Bukhari 5015
references.gist: The Prophet states that Surah Al-Ikhlas is equal to a third of the Quran.

name: The Last Two Verses of Al-Baqarah
summary: The Prophet taught that whoever recites the last two verses of Surah Al-Baqarah at night, they will suffice him.

references.label: Sahih al-Bukhari 4008
references.gist: Abu Mas'ud al-Badri narrates that reciting the last two verses of Surah Al-Baqarah at night suffices the one who recites them.

name: The Quran as an Intercessor
summary: The Prophet taught that the Quran will come on the Day of Resurrection as an intercessor for those who recited it, and described Al-Baqarah and Al-Imran arriving as two clouds, or two shades, pleading for those who recited them.

references.label: Sahih Muslim 804
references.gist: Recite the Quran, for on the Day of Resurrection it comes as an intercessor for those who recited it; Al-Baqarah and Al-Imran come as two clouds pleading for their reciters.

name: The Seven Ahruf
summary: When Umar heard Hisham reciting Surah Al-Furqan differently from how he had been taught, he brought him to the Prophet, who confirmed both recitations and said the Quran was revealed in seven ahruf, so recite whichever is easier.

references.label: Sahih al-Bukhari 4992
references.gist: The Prophet confirms two differing recitations of Surah Al-Furqan as both correct, stating the Quran was revealed in seven ahruf, so recite whichever is easier.

name: Truthfulness
summary: The Prophet taught that truthfulness leads to righteousness and righteousness leads to Paradise, and that a man keeps telling the truth until he is recorded with Allah as truthful; lying leads the opposite way, to wickedness and the Fire, until a man is recorded as a liar.

references.label: Sahih al-Bukhari 6094
references.gist: Truthfulness leads to righteousness and to Paradise, until one is written with Allah as truthful; lying leads to wickedness and the Fire, until one is written as a liar.

name: Backbiting and Suspicion
summary: The Quran instructs believers to avoid much suspicion, since some suspicion is sin, and forbids spying on one another and backbiting one another, in a single passage addressing all three together.

references.label: Surah Al-Hujurat 49:12
references.gist: Instructs avoiding much suspicion, since some of it is sin, and forbids spying and backbiting.

name: Controlling Anger
summary: The Prophet taught that the strong person is not the one who overpowers others, but the one who controls himself when angry.

references.label: Sahih al-Bukhari 6114
references.gist: The strong one is not he who overcomes people by his strength, but he who controls himself while in anger.

name: Mercy and Compassion
summary: The Prophet described the believers, in their mutual mercy, love, and kindness, as resembling one body: when any part of it suffers, the whole body responds with sleeplessness and fever.

references.label: Sahih al-Bukhari 6011
references.gist: The believers in their mutual mercy, love and kindness are like one body: when one part suffers, the whole body shares its sleeplessness and fever.

name: Arrogance (Kibr)
summary: The Prophet taught that no one with the weight of a mustard seed of arrogance in his heart will enter Paradise, and then defined arrogance precisely: rejecting the truth and looking down on people. Asked about liking fine clothing, he answered that Allah is beautiful and loves beauty, which is not what arrogance means.

references.label: Sahih Muslim 91
references.gist: No one with a mustard seed's weight of arrogance enters Paradise; arrogance is defined as rejecting the truth and looking down on people, distinct from liking fine clothing.

name: Envy and Estrangement
summary: The Prophet instructed believers not to envy one another, not to hate one another, and not to cut each other off, but to be brothers as Allah commanded them.

references.label: Sahih al-Bukhari 6064
references.gist: Do not envy one another, do not hate one another, do not cut each other off; be brothers as Allah ordered you.

name: Loving for Others What You Love for Yourself
summary: The Prophet made this a condition of faith itself: none of you believes until he loves for his brother what he loves for himself.

references.label: Sahih al-Bukhari 13
references.gist: None of you believes until he wishes for his brother what he wishes for himself.

name: Haya (Modesty as an Inward Quality)
summary: Passing a man reproaching his brother for being too modest, the Prophet told him to leave him, because haya is part of faith. This is the inward disposition; the separate matter of dress and covering is under Law.

references.label: Sahih al-Bukhari 24
references.gist: The Prophet tells a man reproaching his brother for his modesty to leave him, since haya is part of faith.

name: Seeking Knowledge
summary: The Prophet taught that whoever treads a path in search of knowledge, Allah makes easy for him a path to Paradise.

references.label: Sahih Muslim 2699a
references.gist: Whoever treads a path in search of knowledge, Allah makes easy for him a path to Paradise.

name: Signs for People of Reason
summary: The Quran frames the created world as evidence to be reasoned from: in the creation of the heavens and the earth, and in the alternation of night and day, there are signs for people of understanding.

references.label: Surah Al-Imran 3:190
references.gist: States that in the creation of the heavens and earth, and the alternation of night and day, are signs for people of reason.

name: Every Living Thing From Water
summary: The Quran asks those who disbelieve whether they do not see that the heavens and the earth were one mass before being split apart, and that every living thing was made from water.

references.label: Surah Al-Anbiya 21:30
references.gist: Asks whether the disbelievers do not see that the heavens and earth were one mass then split apart, and that every living thing was made from water.

name: The Stages of Human Creation
summary: The Quran describes human creation in named stages: from an extract of clay, then a drop, then a clinging clot, then a lump, then bones, then the bones clothed with flesh.

references.label: Surah Al-Mu'minun 23:12-14
references.gist: Describes human creation in stages: an extract of clay, a drop, a clinging clot, a lump, bones, then bones clothed with flesh.

name: The Heaven Built and Expanded
summary: The Quran states that Allah built the heaven with might, and that He is expanding it.

references.label: Surah Adh-Dhariyat 51:47
references.gist: States that Allah built the heaven with might and that He is expanding it.

name: The Two Seas and the Barrier
summary: The Quran describes two bodies of water that meet, with a barrier between them that neither transgresses.

references.label: Surah Ar-Rahman 55:19-20
references.gist: Describes two bodies of water meeting, with a barrier between them that they do not cross.

name: Mountains as Pegs
summary: The Quran asks whether Allah has not made the earth a resting place and the mountains as pegs.

references.label: Surah An-Naba 78:6-7
references.gist: Asks whether Allah has not made the earth a bed and the mountains as pegs.

name: The Sun and Moon in Orbit
summary: The Quran states that Allah created the night and the day, the sun and the moon, each one travelling in an orbit.

references.label: Surah Al-Anbiya 21:33
references.gist: States that Allah created the night, day, sun and moon, each travelling in an orbit.

name: The Seven Heavens
summary: The Quran states that Allah created seven heavens in layers, and invites the reader to look again and again for any flaw in the creation of the Most Merciful, since none will be found.

references.label: Surah Al-Mulk 67:3
references.gist: States Allah created seven heavens in layers and challenges the reader to look for any flaw in the creation.

name: Shukr (Gratitude)
summary: Allah states directly that if people are grateful, He will increase them, and that if they are ungrateful, His punishment is severe.

references.label: Surah Ibrahim 14:7
references.gist: States that if you are grateful, Allah will increase you, and that if you are ungrateful, His punishment is severe.

name: Dhikr (Remembrance of Allah)
summary: The Quran states that hearts find rest in the remembrance of Allah. The Prophet taught that whoever says 'SubhanAllah wa bihamdihi' a hundred times in a day has his sins forgiven, even if they were like the foam of the sea.

references.label: Surah Ar-Ra'd 13:28
references.gist: States that hearts find rest in the remembrance of Allah.

references.label: Sahih al-Bukhari 6405
references.gist: Whoever says SubhanAllah wa bihamdihi a hundred times a day is forgiven his sins, even if they were like the foam of the sea.

name: Tasbih After Each Prayer
summary: The Prophet taught saying 'SubhanAllah' thirty-three times, 'Alhamdulillah' thirty-three times, and 'Allahu akbar' thirty-four times after every obligatory prayer, telling those who do so that they will never be disappointed.

references.label: Sahih Muslim 596a
references.gist: Teaches saying tasbih thirty-three times, tahmid thirty-three times, and takbir thirty-four times after every prescribed prayer.

name: Salawat Upon the Prophet
summary: The Quran states that Allah and His angels send blessings upon the Prophet, and instructs the believers to invoke blessings upon him and greet him with peace.

references.label: Surah Al-Ahzab 33:56
references.gist: States Allah and His angels send blessings upon the Prophet, and instructs believers to invoke blessings and peace upon him.

name: Ghayb (Belief in the Unseen)
summary: The Quran opens by describing the guided as those who believe in the unseen, ghayb, naming it in the same breath as establishing prayer and giving charity, as a defining mark of true faith.

references.label: Surah Al-Baqarah 2:3
references.gist: Describes the guided as those who believe in the unseen, establish prayer, and give from what Allah has provided them.

name: Wahy (How Revelation Came)
summary: Asked how revelation came to him, the Prophet described two forms: sometimes like the ringing of a bell, the hardest form, and sometimes an angel appearing as a man to speak to him directly. Aisha observed that on a cold day, his forehead would still be dripping with sweat when a revelation ended.

references.label: Sahih al-Bukhari 2
references.gist: Describes revelation coming sometimes like the ringing of a bell, and sometimes as an angel in the form of a man; Aisha notes his sweating even in cold weather.

name: Isti'adhah (Seeking Refuge Before Reciting)
summary: The Quran instructs that when reciting it, one should first seek refuge with Allah from Satan, the accursed, the basis for saying 'a'udhu billahi min ash-shaytan ir-rajim' before recitation.

references.label: Surah An-Nahl 16:98
references.gist: Instructs seeking refuge with Allah from Satan, the accursed, before reciting the Quran.

name: Dua for Increase in Knowledge
summary: Immediately after instructing the Prophet not to rush ahead of the revelation as it is conveyed to him, the Quran teaches him to pray, 'My Lord, increase me in knowledge.'

references.label: Surah Ta-Ha 20:114
references.gist: Teaches the prayer, my Lord, increase me in knowledge, given directly after instructing the Prophet not to rush ahead of the revelation.

name: Justice ('Adl)
summary: The Quran commands standing firm for justice as a witness for Allah, even if the testimony is against oneself, one's parents, or one's close relatives.

references.label: Surah An-Nisa 4:135
references.gist: Commands standing firm for justice as witnesses for Allah, even against oneself, one's parents, or close relatives.

name: Forgiving Others
summary: The Quran, in the passage addressing a slander against Aisha, instructs those wronged to pardon and overlook, asking directly: do you not love that Allah should forgive you?

references.label: Surah An-Nur 24:22
references.gist: Instructs letting wrongs be pardoned and overlooked, asking whether one does not love that Allah should forgive them.

name: Keeping Promises
summary: The Quran instructs honoring one's pledges, stating plainly that a person will be held to account for them.

references.label: Surah Al-Isra 17:34
references.gist: Instructs honoring pledges, stating a person will be held accountable for them.

name: Humility
summary: The Prophet taught that no one humbles himself for the sake of Allah without Allah raising his standing.

references.label: Sahih Muslim 2588
references.gist: No one humbles himself for Allah's sake without Allah raising his standing among people.

name: Smiling Is Charity
summary: The Prophet taught that smiling in your brother's face is an act of charity, grouped alongside commanding good and forbidding wrong.

references.label: Jami at-Tirmidhi 1956
references.gist: Smiling in your brother's face is charity; commanding good and forbidding evil is charity. Graded hasan by at-Tirmidhi.

name: Ikhlas (Sincerity)
summary: The Quran states plainly that people were commanded only to worship Allah, sincere in devotion to Him alone, alongside establishing prayer and giving charity.

references.label: Surah Al-Bayyinah 98:5
references.gist: States people were commanded only to worship Allah with sincere devotion, establish prayer, and give charity.

name: The Punishment for Theft
summary: The Quran prescribes cutting off the hand of the male or female thief as a deterrent punishment from Allah for what they have done.

references.label: Surah Al-Ma'idah 5:38
references.gist: Prescribes cutting off the hand of the male or female thief as a deterrent punishment from Allah.

name: Shura (Consultation)
summary: The Quran describes conducting affairs by mutual consultation as a defining trait of the believers, named alongside responding to their Lord, establishing prayer, and giving charity.

references.label: Surah Ash-Shura 42:38
references.gist: Describes the believers as those who conduct their affairs by mutual consultation, alongside prayer and charity.

name: Expiation for Breaking Oaths
summary: The Quran sets the expiation for a broken oath: feeding ten poor people as one would feed one's own family, or clothing them, or freeing someone from bondage; and for whoever cannot afford this, fasting three days instead.

references.label: Surah Al-Ma'idah 5:89
references.gist: Sets the expiation for a broken oath as feeding or clothing ten poor people, or freeing someone from bondage, or fasting three days if unable.

name: Rights of Those Held in Bondage
summary: The Quran instructs granting a contract of freedom to any bondsperson who requests one and shows good in them, and to help fund it from Allah's own wealth. The Prophet went further, calling them brothers under one's authority, to be fed and clothed the same as oneself, and not burdened beyond their capacity.

references.label: Surah An-Nur 24:33
references.gist: Instructs granting a freedom contract to any bondsperson who requests one and shows good, helping fund it from Allah's wealth.

references.label: Sahih al-Bukhari 2545
references.gist: Calls those in bondage brothers under one's authority, to be fed and clothed as oneself and not burdened beyond capacity.

name: The Bee and Its Honey
summary: The Quran describes Allah inspiring the bee to make its home in the mountains, in trees, and in what people build, producing from its body a drink of varying colors in which there is healing for people.

references.label: Surah An-Nahl 16:68-69
references.gist: Describes Allah inspiring the bee to build its home in mountains, trees, and structures, producing a drink of varying colors with healing in it.

name: Winds, Rain, and Dead Land Revived
summary: The Quran describes Allah sending the winds as bearers of good news ahead of His mercy, sending down pure water from the sky to give life to a dead land.

references.label: Surah Al-Furqan 25:48
references.gist: Describes Allah sending the winds as bearers of good news ahead of His mercy, and sending down pure water from the sky.

name: Ships Sailing the Sea
summary: The Quran names ships that sail the sea carrying what benefits people among the signs meant for those who understand.

references.label: Surah Al-Baqarah 2:164
references.gist: Names ships sailing the sea carrying what benefits people among the signs for people of understanding.

name: Sleep as a Sign
summary: The Quran names sleep, by night and by day, alongside the human pursuit of provision, as one of Allah's signs.

references.label: Surah Ar-Rum 30:23
references.gist: Names sleep by night and day, and the pursuit of provision, among Allah's signs.

name: The Diversity of Languages and Colors
summary: The Quran names the diversity of human languages and colors, alongside the creation of the heavens and the earth, as a sign for people of knowledge.

references.label: Surah Ar-Rum 30:22
references.gist: Names the diversity of languages and colors, alongside the creation of the heavens and earth, as a sign for people of knowledge.

name: Tawbah (Repentance)
summary: The Quran addresses those who have transgressed against themselves directly, telling them not to despair of Allah's mercy, since Allah forgives all sins and is the Forgiving, the Merciful.

references.label: Surah Az-Zumar 39:53
references.gist: Tells those who have transgressed against themselves not to despair of Allah's mercy, since Allah forgives all sins.

name: Allah's Mercy Precedes His Wrath
summary: The Prophet taught that Allah wrote, upon Himself, that His mercy prevails over His wrath.

references.label: Sahih al-Bukhari 7404
references.gist: Allah wrote upon Himself that His mercy prevails over His wrath.

name: Closeness to Allah Through Voluntary Worship
summary: In a hadith qudsi, Allah declares war on whoever shows hostility to His close servant, and describes drawing a servant near through obligatory duties first, then continued voluntary acts, until Allah becomes, as the hadith describes it, the hearing with which he hears and the sight with which he sees.

references.label: Sahih al-Bukhari 6502
references.gist: Allah declares war on whoever shows hostility to His close servant, and describes drawing near through obligatory duties then voluntary acts, becoming the servant's hearing, sight, hand, and foot.

name: Witr Prayer
summary: The Prophet instructed making witr the last prayer of the night.

references.label: Sahih al-Bukhari 998
references.gist: The Prophet instructs making witr the last prayer of the night.

name: I'tikaf
summary: Aisha narrates that the Prophet observed i'tikaf, seclusion for worship in the mosque, in the last ten days of Ramadan until his death, and that his wives continued the practice after him.

references.label: Sahih al-Bukhari 2026
references.gist: The Prophet observed i'tikaf in the last ten days of Ramadan until his death; his wives continued the practice afterward.

name: The Mu'awwidhatayn Before Sleep
summary: Aisha narrates that whenever the Prophet went to bed, he would recite Al-Ikhlas, Al-Falaq, and An-Nas, blow into his cupped hands, and pass them over as much of his body as he could reach.

references.label: Sahih al-Bukhari 5748
references.gist: Whenever the Prophet went to bed, he recited Al-Ikhlas, Al-Falaq, and An-Nas, blew into his hands, and passed them over his body.

name: Safety From One's Tongue and Hand
summary: The Prophet defined a Muslim, at its simplest, as one from whose tongue and hand other people are safe.

references.label: Sahih al-Bukhari 10
references.gist: A Muslim is one from whose tongue and hand other people are safe.

name: Rifq (Gentleness)
summary: The Prophet taught that Allah is gentle and loves gentleness, granting through it what He does not grant through harshness.

references.label: Sahih Muslim 2593
references.gist: Allah is gentle and loves gentleness, granting through it what He does not grant through harshness.

name: Bribery
summary: The Prophet cursed both the one who offers a bribe in a judgment and the one who accepts it.

references.label: Jami at-Tirmidhi 1336
references.gist: The Prophet curses the one who bribes and the one who takes the bribe in a judgment. Graded hasan by at-Tirmidhi.

name: Hoarding for Profit (Ihtikar)
summary: The Prophet stated plainly that whoever hoards goods to drive up their price is a sinner.

references.label: Sahih Muslim 1605
references.gist: Whoever hoards goods to drive up prices is a sinner.

name: Planting as Charity
summary: The Prophet taught that when a Muslim plants a tree or sows a crop, and a bird, a person, or an animal eats from it, it counts as charity for the one who planted it, a right extended even to creatures with no direct claim.

references.label: Sahih al-Bukhari 2320
references.gist: There is no Muslim who plants a tree or sows seed, then a bird, person, or animal eats from it, but it is charity for him.

name: Lightning, Fear and Hope
summary: The Quran names lightning, showing itself to people as both fear and hope, among Allah's signs.

references.label: Surah Ar-Rum 30:24
references.gist: Names lightning, showing itself to people as fear and hope, among Allah's signs.

name: Night Passing Into Day
summary: The Quran states, addressing Allah directly, that He causes the night to pass into the day and the day to pass into the night.

references.label: Surah Al-Imran 3:27
references.gist: States that Allah causes the night to pass into the day and the day to pass into the night.

name: Everything Created in Pairs
summary: The Quran glorifies Allah as the One who created all things in pairs, what the earth produces, people themselves, and things not yet known.

references.label: Surah Ya-Sin 36:36
references.gist: Glorifies Allah as the One who created all things in pairs, what the earth produces, people, and what is not yet known.

name: Grain, Dates, and Gardens
summary: The Quran describes Allah sending down rain that produces green stalks and clustered grain, date palms with low-hanging clusters, and gardens of grapes, olives, and pomegranates, alike yet unlike.

references.label: Surah Al-An'am 6:99
references.gist: Describes rain producing grain, date-palm clusters, and gardens of grapes, olives, and pomegranates, similar yet different.

name: Iron Sent Down
summary: The Quran describes Allah sending down iron, in which is great might and benefit for people.

references.label: Surah Al-Hadid 57:25
references.gist: Describes Allah sending down iron, in which is great might and benefits for people.

name: Love of the Prophet
summary: The Prophet taught that none of you truly believes until he loves him more than his own father, his own child, and all of mankind.

references.label: Sahih al-Bukhari 15
references.gist: None of you truly believes until I am more beloved to him than his father, his child, and all mankind.

name: Closer Than the Jugular Vein
summary: The Quran states that Allah created mankind and knows what their souls whisper to them, and that He is closer to a person than their own jugular vein.

references.label: Surah Qaf 50:16
references.gist: States Allah created mankind, knows what their souls whisper to them, and is closer to them than their jugular vein.

name: The Dua of Yunus
summary: Yunus's prayer from inside the fish, 'there is no god but You, glory be to You, I have certainly done wrong,' is recorded in the Quran itself. The Prophet taught that no Muslim ever supplicates with it in any matter without Allah answering him.

references.label: Surah Al-Anbiya 21:87
references.gist: Records Yunus's prayer from inside the fish: there is no god but You, glory be to You, I have certainly done wrong.

references.label: Jami at-Tirmidhi 3505
references.gist: No Muslim ever supplicates with Yunus's dua in any matter without Allah answering him.

name: Musa's Dua for Ease
summary: Sent to confront Pharaoh, Musa asked Allah to expand his chest, ease his task, and remove the impediment from his tongue so people would understand his speech, a dua widely recited before any difficult or daunting undertaking.

references.label: Surah Ta-Ha 20:25-28
references.gist: Musa asks Allah to expand his chest, ease his task, and remove the impediment from his tongue so people understand his speech.

name: Actions Are by Intentions
summary: The Prophet opened one of the most foundational hadith in Islam with this principle: deeds are judged by intentions, and each person gets only what he intended. Whoever emigrates for worldly gain or to marry, rather than for Allah, gets only that.

references.label: Sahih al-Bukhari 1
references.gist: Deeds are judged by intentions, and each person gets what he intended; whoever emigrates for worldly gain or marriage gets only that.

name: Generosity
summary: The Quran states that true righteousness is never attained until one gives from what one loves, and that whatever is given is fully known to Allah.

references.label: Surah Al-Imran 3:92
references.gist: States that righteousness is never attained until one gives from what one loves, and that Allah fully knows whatever is given.

name: Avoiding Wastefulness
summary: The Quran instructs eating and drinking without excess, stating plainly that Allah does not love the wasteful.

references.label: Surah Al-A'raf 7:31
references.gist: Instructs eating and drinking without excess, stating Allah does not love the wasteful.

name: Consistency in Good Deeds
summary: Aisha narrates that the most beloved deeds to Allah were the most consistent ones, even if small, and that one should only take on what can be sustained.

references.label: Sahih al-Bukhari 6465
references.gist: The most beloved deeds to Allah are the most consistent, even if small.

name: Slander (Qadhf)
summary: The Quran sets a demanding evidentiary standard for accusing a chaste person of unlawful sexual relations: whoever makes the accusation without producing four witnesses is to be given eighty lashes.

references.label: Surah An-Nur 24:4
references.gist: Those who accuse chaste women without producing four witnesses are to be given eighty lashes.

name: Privacy and Entering Others' Homes
summary: The Quran instructs believers not to enter any house other than their own until they have asked permission and greeted its occupants.

references.label: Surah An-Nur 24:27
references.gist: Instructs not entering any house other than one's own until asking permission and greeting its occupants.

name: Rights of the Wayfarer
summary: The Quran names the traveler stranded far from home, the wayfarer, alongside relatives and the needy, as someone owed their due, in the same breath as a warning against wastefulness.

references.label: Surah Al-Isra 17:26
references.gist: Instructs giving close relatives, the needy, and the wayfarer their due, and not spending wastefully.

name: The Constellations
summary: The Quran states that Allah placed constellations in the sky and adorned it for those who look at it.

references.label: Surah Al-Hijr 15:16
references.gist: States Allah placed constellations in the sky and adorned it for those who look at it.

name: The Trust (Al-Amanah)
summary: The Quran describes Allah offering the Trust to the heavens, the earth, and the mountains, who all declined to bear it out of fear, while mankind took it on, described in the same verse as wronging themselves and ignorant of what they were taking on.

references.label: Surah Al-Ahzab 33:72
references.gist: The heavens, earth, and mountains decline to bear the Trust out of fear, while mankind takes it on, described as wronging themselves and ignorant of the consequences.

name: No Soul Burdened Beyond Its Capacity
summary: The Quran states outright that Allah does not require of any soul more than it is able to bear.

references.label: Surah Al-Baqarah 2:286
references.gist: States Allah does not require of any soul more than it is able to bear.

name: Dua for the Deceased
summary: The Prophet's own supplication over the deceased: forgive him, have mercy on him, grant him well-being and pardon, make his grave spacious, cleanse him of faults, and admit him to Paradise, protected from the trial of the grave and the torment of the Fire.

references.label: Sahih Muslim 963a
references.gist: The Prophet's supplication over the deceased: forgive him, have mercy on him, cleanse him of his faults, and admit him to Paradise, protected from the grave and the Fire.

name: Dua Between the Adhan and Iqamah
summary: The Prophet taught that a supplication made between the call to prayer and the start of the prayer itself is not rejected.

references.label: Jami at-Tirmidhi 212
references.gist: A supplication made between the adhan and the iqamah is not rejected.

name: Turning Away From the Ignorant
summary: The Quran instructs a threefold response to how others behave: show grace, enjoin what is right, and turn away from those who act with ignorance, rather than answer them in kind.

references.label: Surah Al-A'raf 7:199
references.gist: Instructs showing grace, enjoining what is right, and turning away from those who act with ignorance.

name: Good Character on the Scale
summary: The Prophet taught that nothing will be heavier on the believer's scale on the Day of Judgment than good character.

references.label: Jami at-Tirmidhi 2002
references.gist: Nothing is heavier on the believer's scale on the Day of Judgment than good character.

name: The Sanctity of Human Life (Prohibition of Killing)
summary: The Quran states plainly the base prohibition beneath the whole framework of retaliation: do not take a life that Allah has made sacred, except by right.

references.label: Surah Al-Isra 17:33
references.gist: States the prohibition against taking a life Allah has made sacred, except by right.

name: Even the Fingertips Remade
summary: Answering the question of whether people think their bones will not be reassembled, the Quran states that Allah is able to remake even a person's fingertips, precisely.

references.label: Surah Al-Qiyamah 75:3-4
references.gist: Answers doubt that bones will be reassembled: Allah is able to remake even a person's fingertips.

name: Birds Held Aloft in the Sky
summary: The Quran asks whether people have not seen birds gliding in the open sky, held up by nothing but Allah.

references.label: Surah An-Nahl 16:79
references.gist: Asks whether people have not seen birds gliding in the sky, held up by nothing but Allah.

name: The Sky Raised Without Pillars
summary: The Quran states that Allah raised the heavens without any pillars visible to the eye.

references.label: Surah Ar-Ra'd 13:2
references.gist: States Allah raised the heavens without pillars visible to the eye.

name: Shortening Prayer While Traveling (Qasr)
summary: The Quran permits shortening the prayer while traveling. Ibn Umar narrates that he never saw the Prophet pray more than two rak'ahs on a journey, a practice Abu Bakr, Umar, and Uthman continued after him.

references.label: Surah An-Nisa 4:101
references.gist: Permits shortening the prayer when traveling through the land.

references.label: Sahih al-Bukhari 1102
references.gist: Ibn Umar narrates the Prophet never offered more than two rak'ahs on a journey, a practice Abu Bakr, Umar, and Uthman continued.

name: Istisqa, the Prayer for Rain
summary: The Prophet went out specifically to pray for rain, facing the qibla, turning his cloak inside out, and praying two rak'ahs with audible recitation.

references.label: Sahih al-Bukhari 1024
references.gist: The Prophet went out to pray for rain, facing the qibla, turning his cloak inside out, and praying two rak'ahs with audible recitation.

name: The People of Saba (Sheba)
summary: The people of Saba were given a sign in their own homeland: two orchards, one on each side, with the command to eat from their Lord's provision and be grateful, in a good land under a forgiving Lord. They turned away, so a devastating flood was sent against them, their orchards replaced with bitter fruit, fruitless bushes, and sparse thorny trees. When they even asked for their trade journeys between towns to be made longer, wronging themselves, Allah scattered them completely and turned them into a cautionary tale told among people.

references.label: Surah Saba 34:15-19
references.gist: The people of Saba are given fertile orchards and told to be grateful; they turn away, are struck by a flood, and are scattered as a cautionary tale.

chapters.heading: A Sign in Their Own Land
chapters.narrative: The people of Saba had a sign in their own dwelling place: two orchards, one on the right and one on the left. They were told to eat from what their Lord had provided and be grateful to Him, for theirs was a good land and a forgiving Lord.

references.label: Surah Saba 34:15
references.gist: The people of Saba are given two flourishing orchards and told to eat from their Lord's provision and be grateful.

chapters.heading: Turning Away and the Flood
chapters.narrative: They turned away from gratitude, so Allah sent against them a devastating flood, and replaced their two fertile orchards with others bearing bitter fruit, fruitless bushes, and a few sparse thorny trees.

references.label: Surah Saba 34:16
references.gist: The people of Saba turn away, and a devastating flood replaces their orchards with bitter fruit and thorny plants.

chapters.heading: Scattered as a Cautionary Tale
chapters.narrative: The Quran notes they had once had towns close together along their trade routes, with journeys made easy and secure, but they asked instead that their journeys be made longer, wronging themselves. So Allah scattered them completely, turning them into stories told as a warning to others.

references.label: Surah Saba 34:18-19
references.gist: The people of Saba, once given secure and easy trade routes, ask for longer journeys instead, so Allah scatters them and turns them into a cautionary tale.

name: The Man Who Discarded Allah's Signs
summary: The Quran tells of a man given Allah's signs who cast them aside, so Satan took hold of him and he became lost. Had Allah willed, he could have been raised by these signs, but he clung to the earth and followed his own desire instead. The Quran compares him to a dog: pant if you chase it away, and it still pants if you leave it alone. The Quran does not name him.

references.label: Surah Al-A'raf 7:175-176
references.gist: A man given Allah's signs casts them aside and is taken hold of by Satan; he clings to the earth and follows his desire, compared to a dog that pants either way.

name: Jihad (Striving in Allah's Cause)
summary: The Quran promises that those who strive in Allah's cause will be guided to His ways, and that Allah is with those who do good. The word's root meaning is exertion or struggle, of which armed struggle under specific legal conditions is one form among others, not its only sense.

references.label: Surah Al-Ankabut 29:69
references.gist: Promises that those who strive in Allah's cause will be guided to His ways, and that Allah is with those who do good.

name: Ihsan (Excellence in Worship)
summary: When Jibril asked the Prophet to define ihsan, he answered: that you worship Allah as though you see Him, and though you do not see Him, He sees you. This is the third term the foundational hadith distinguishes, alongside Islam and Iman.

references.label: Sahih Muslim 8
references.gist: Defines ihsan as worshipping Allah as though you see Him, and though you do not see Him, He sees you.

name: Respecting Elders
summary: The Prophet said that whoever does not show mercy to the young among us, and does not recognize the right of the elderly among us, is not one of us.

references.label: Sunan Abi Dawud 4943
references.gist: Whoever does not show mercy to the young and does not recognize the right of the elderly is not one of us.

name: Al-Birr: What Righteousness Actually Is
summary: In one of the Quran's most comprehensive single verses, righteousness is defined not as which direction one faces in prayer, but as belief in Allah, the Last Day, the angels, the Books, and the prophets; giving cherished wealth to relatives, orphans, the poor, travelers, beggars, and toward freeing captives; establishing prayer and giving zakat; keeping one's word; and being patient in hardship, adversity, and conflict.

references.label: Surah Al-Baqarah 2:177
references.gist: Defines righteousness comprehensively: belief in Allah, the Last Day, angels, Books, and prophets; charity toward relatives, orphans, the poor, travelers, beggars, and captives; prayer, zakat, keeping promises, and patience in hardship.

name: Washing the Deceased
summary: The Prophet instructed the women washing his own daughter's body to wash her three times, five, or more if needed, with water and lote-tree leaves, finishing with camphor, and to inform him once done.

references.label: Sahih al-Bukhari 1253
references.gist: The Prophet instructs the women washing his daughter's body to wash her three or five times with water and lote-tree leaves, finishing with camphor.

name: Kafan (Shrouding the Deceased)
summary: Aisha narrates that the Prophet himself was shrouded in three plain white Yemeni cotton cloths, with no shirt and no turban among them.

references.label: Sahih al-Bukhari 1264
references.gist: Aisha narrates the Prophet was shrouded in three plain white Yemeni cotton cloths, with no shirt or turban.

name: The Widow's Waiting Period
summary: The Quran sets a widow's waiting period after her husband's death at four months and ten days, distinct from the waiting period after a divorce.

references.label: Surah Al-Baqarah 2:234
references.gist: Sets a widow's waiting period after her husband's death at four months and ten days.

name: The Purpose Behind Jinn and Mankind
summary: The Quran states directly that Allah did not create jinn and mankind except to worship Him.

references.label: Surah Adh-Dhariyat 51:56
references.gist: States Allah did not create jinn and mankind except to worship Him.

name: Dua for Good in This World and the Next
summary: One of the most widely recited duas in the Quran itself: Our Lord, grant us good in this world and good in the Hereafter, and protect us from the punishment of the Fire.

references.label: Surah Al-Baqarah 2:201
references.gist: Our Lord, grant us good in this world and good in the Hereafter, and protect us from the punishment of the Fire.
